question: In a patient with simple central obesity and no clinical features suggesting a secondary cause, the minimum investigation set should include fasting lipid profile and fasting plasma glucose (or HbA1c), but thyroid function tests and cortisol are NOT required unless specific clinical features are present.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. In the absence of clinical pointers (e.g., cold intolerance/bradycardia for hypothyroidism; purple striae/proximal weakness for Cushing), TFTs and cortisol are not part of the routine obesity investigation set. Investigations should be targeted by clinical findings.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Routine investigations screen for metabolic complications (dyslipidaemia, dysglycaemia, fatty liver). TFTs and cortisol tests are reserved for patients with clinical features suggesting hypothyroidism or Cushing syndrome respectively — not done routinely in all obese patients.
